opportunities.title: Competition search rejects exact Unicode names and overcounts substitutions — fix proposal
opportunities.summary: I found two reproducible correctness defects in the competition-name search in this repository at commit `e1ff2faadd438c933e69f580b173d917eeb2da1d`. 1. `calculateLevenshtein("Copa América", "Copa América")` returns **13**, although an exact match should return **0**. Consequently, a local search index containing that exact competition rejects the same query. The row is sized and returned using UTF-8 byte length, while the loops advance by Unicode code points. 2. `calculateLevenshtein("cat", "bat")` returns **2** instead of **1**. The recurrence omits the substitution cost. This can reject queries within the intended spelling-error tolerance or rank matches incorrectly. I have prepared a small patch that uses code points consistently, restores substitution costs, and makes the tolerance threshold use the same unit. It includes 20 local test cases: 11 fail on the original code and all 20 pass after the fix. `go vet ./...` also passes. The work was prepared with AI assistance and independently reviewed. opportunities.summary: ## Bug On `7163538913e15dd86534b41dc695e2a5639c0774`, interrupting the interactive `omi auth login` method-selection prompt is handled as an unexpected exception: stderr contains `omi: unexpected error: ` (empty reason) and the process exits 1. The entry point already intends to handle KeyboardInterrupt/EOFError with `Aborted.` and exit 130, but Click converts prompt interruption into `click.Abort`, which falls through to the generic exception handler. ## Reproduction and evidence Run `omi auth login` in an interactive terminal and cancel at `Choose 1 or 2 [1]:` using Ctrl-C or EOF. Automated verification exercises the actual `main()` entry point and real login prompt, substituting a terminal-like stdin whose readline raises KeyboardInterrupt or EOFError. It does not contact live authentication services or use credentials. A candidate one-line fix includes `click.Abort` in the existing interruption handler. Two parametrized regression cases assert exit 130, `Aborted.`, and absence of `unexpected error`. opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
